rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's fourteen builder trees go (jacarandas, eucalyptus and ficus along the back fences, a queen palm 3 m from a house front, others by the seating); five come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the adirondack chair, the grill, the swing set, on the open lot corner, and one back yard.

trees.why: the back yard with the adirondack chair (1.3 m off): a coral tree to sit under
the south-west yard with the kettle grill (1.7 m off): a jacaranda over the cook
the yard with the swing set (2.8 m off): shade over the swings
the open lot corner at the south-west, 24 m from the walls: an old ficus
the east back yard of the north row, 7 m from the house: the yard's tree
